title: Decisions
bridge: C++ uses `if (...) { } else if (...) { } else { }` with `&&` (and), `||` (or), `!` (not). Comparisons are `== != < > <= >=`. `switch` works on whole numbers and chars. Careful: `if (x = 5)` *assigns* and is always true; you meant `==`.

exercises.title: Grades
exercises.prompt: Write std::string grade(int score): A for 80+, B for 65+, C for 50+, otherwise F.

exercises.title: Leap years
exercises.prompt: Write bool isLeap(int year): divisible by 4, except centuries, which must be divisible by 400.

tests.hint_if_fail: 1900 is a century not divisible by 400.

choices: Sets x to 5, and is always true

quiz.q: Forgetting break in a switch case...
choices: falls through into the next case
quiz.why: Execution carries on into the next case.

explain: Explain decisions to someone who has never programmed, in your own words, with an example you make up.
